CHIEF COMPLAINT
Hepatitis C positive on screening lab work.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a previously healthy individual who presented after hepatitis C antibody testing came back positive during routine physical examination. Patient reports feeling fine with no symptoms. This is the first time hepatitis C has been diagnosed. Patient has a significant past history of intravenous drug use but has been clean for over 15 years. Patient understands that hepatitis C is a viral infection affecting the liver and acknowledges that most patients do not develop symptoms for years after infection.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies current symptoms related to liver disease or hepatitis C. No jaundice reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No significant medical conditions other than hepatitis C diagnosis.

MEDICATIONS
Patient denies current medications.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Hypertension, diabetes, and depression.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient has a remote history of intravenous drug use, clean for over 15 years. Current alcohol use: occasional beer, daily but significantly reduced from past use. Tobacco use: 1-2 cigarettes per day, has cut down significantly but continues to struggle with cessation. Married with children.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vitals: All within normal limits. General: No distress, no jaundice. Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm with grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur. Pulmonary: Clear lungs without wheezes, rales, or rhonchi. Abdomen: Bowel sounds present, soft, no hepatosplenomegaly. Neurologic: No gait disturbance or edema noted.

RESULTS
Hepatitis C antibody: Positive. Liver panel: AST elevated at 39 U/L; ALT, albumin, and total bilirubin within normal limits.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Hepatitis C infection confirmed by positive HCV antibody. Plan to confirm diagnosis with additional blood work including HCV RNA and HCV genotype. Will assess severity of liver disease with ultrasound elastography to evaluate for fibrosis. Family screening recommended with HCV antibody testing for wife and children. Follow-up appointment in 3 weeks to review results and determine treatment plan. Nurse will provide orders and assist with scheduling.
